prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1221; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Good. Can you tell me in your own words what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was stopped at a red light in Baytown, waiting to turn left. The car behind me didn't slow down in time and hit me from the back. It wasn't a huge impact, but it was enough to jolt me forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Were you able to drive your vehicle afterward?

A: Yes, it was still drivable, so I pulled over to the side of the road and waited for the police to arrive.

Q: Did you go to a doctor or the emergency room?

A: I went to urgent care that same evening. My neck and upper back were really sore, and I had headaches the next morning. They diagnosed me with whiplash and told me to take it easy.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: Still stiff in the neck, especially when I turn my head to check traffic. I've been going to physical therapy twice a week, and it's helping some, but I still can't sleep through the night without waking up in pain.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: A few days right after the accident, and I've been limiting my hours since then because sitting at my desk for long stretches aggravates it.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Just that I want to be sure my medical bills and the repairs to my car get covered. I've kept all my receipts and paperwork.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up once we've reviewed everything. Have a good day.

A: You too, thanks.
